image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Stacked area chart.

2. **Layout techniques**:  
- Uses **stacking** to show multiple outcome categories over time.  
- No faceting or small multiples; all categories appear in a single panel.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Year | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Number of animals / outcomes count | Quantitative | Position on y-axis; area height/thickness |
| Outcome category (Euthanized, Adopted, Returned to owner, Transferred to rescue, Released, Lost or died) | Categorical/nominal | Stacked area segments; direct text labels inside areas |
| Animal type (dogs and cats combined) | Categorical/nominal | Mentioned in title only; not separately encoded visually |

comments.raw_comment: First and foremost, we notice a steady decline in euthanization throughout the past few years. This is due to an increase in pet safety laws and PETA's growing influence. Overall, the downward trend is due to a decrease in animals going to this Dallas shelter. This can be attributed to movies like A Dog's Purpose and the cost of pet food. The sudden increase of pets in 2017 is due to Hurricane Harvey. The hurricane did not hit Dallas, and so, animals from shelters in the area that was hit were transferred to other shelters around the country (and even more so through the state). As a result, people were moved to adopt more sad, poor animals homeless by the hurricane. We wonder why there was an increase in animals who were released and what that means. We also are curious to know what this graph would look like today. Would there be an increase in adoptions? Would there be a decrease in animals arriving to the shelter? We love the title from Mrs. Lane from ELP Teacher: "It's Raining Cats and Dogs"

We noticed a steady decrease in all categories up until the year 2016, where everything but adoption rates and returning rates to owners decreased, and the aforementioned categories rose with the rise in populations entering the Dallas animal services. Other things that are notable could be the increase of released animals starting from 2014 and the spike and fall of transferring animals to rescue from 2017 to 2018. We wonder if these things could be affected by weather outbreaks and modern social influences. Outbreaks of tornadoes and hurricanes could affect the population levels entering into the Dallas animal services because of the destruction of houses. The destruction brought with these natural disasters could misplace thousands of animals from their homes. The loss of their owner's life during these events could also be attributed to this as well. This could explain the spike in population as well as the rise in the returning rate. Modern entertainment, such as movies could affect this as well, such as the release of the movie "A Dog's Purpose" in 2016. Movies similar to the previous one could influence the viewers to make the decision to adopt as well as influence society to be open to rescuing animals.

comments.raw_comment: In this graph, I notice that the outcome for the shelter dogs and cats in Dallas Animal Services, as displayed by the title, that have been euthanized has gradually decreased and the rate of adoption overall has increased from 2009-2017. These points are symbolized with the blue representing animals that were euthanized, the dark blue line representing animals that have been lost, died, or released, and the tan color representing animals that have been adopted or transferred. The y-axis represents the amount of animals in the shelters and the x-axis represents the year. I wonder what might have caused these results, and why the statistics for both cats and dogs have been grouped together? Maybe as time passed more awareness for dogs and cats in shelters has been raised and therefore adoption rates have increased. Dogs and cats might have been grouped together because they make up most of the animal shelters in Texas. Possible Title: "Clearing the Shelters through Adoption"
